meta.description: Located and regional hazards for landing and surface work at the lunar south pole: tectonic scarps, seismicity, slopes, regolith, plume, dust, radiation, micrometeoroids, thermal extremes and lighting.
meta.coordinate_convention: Decimal degrees; latitude south negative; longitude east-positive; lon_east_180 (-180..180) and lon_east_360 (0..360). Where the notes gave only one form the other was computed during conversion (+/-360).
meta.validation: Copied from research notes of 2026-11-14. Not validated by the science lead.
source_meta_notes: Values copied from research notes of 2026-11-14; not independently validated.

Evidence labels (as in the notes): ESTABLISHED = measured / documented in primary or official sources; MODEL = result of a published simulation, not a measurement; CONTESTED = published but disputed; SPECULATIVE = hypothesis without supporting data. INTERPRETATION / PROPOSAL are used where the notes use them.

Item 'category' values: hazard_scarp, hazard_seismic, hazard_terrain, hazard_regolith, hazard_plume, hazard_dust, hazard_radiation, hazard_micrometeoroid, hazard_thermal, hazard_lighting, science_feature, crater_age, science_objective, geologic_product, astrobiology, planetary_protection, site_ranking.
There is NO evidence of indigenous lunar life. 'Possible bacteria' refers to forward contamination by terrestrial microbes (modelled dormant survival), not detection of lunar organisms.
No rule forbids landing in or near south-polar PSRs; Category IIb (south of 79 S) means documentation, not prohibition.
None of the published rankings is official; NASA has published no site scores.

properties.notes: Lies within the de Gerlache Rim 2 candidate region. One relocated N9 solution lies within ~24 km of the de Gerlache scarps (source not uniquely determined).
~30 km from Nobile Rim 1; a PSR on the Nobile rim within 20 km of the scarp is landslide-susceptible.

properties.mapped_length_scr: ~582 km of lobate scarps mapped in Krasilnikov et al. Zenodo data v1.3

items.name: Modelled shallow moonquake on a polar scarp

properties.shaking: strong-to-moderate to >= ~40 km; moderate-to-light beyond ~50 km
properties.landslide_trigger: ~2.3% of lunar g (1.62 m/s2) for a 1 m slab on >30 deg slopes at low cohesion
properties.susceptible_areas_C_0_1_kPa: large portions of Shackleton interior walls, its NW rim and parts of Connecting Ridge near the rim; interior walls in Nobile Rim 1; a PSR north of de Gerlache Rim 2; a PSR on the Nobile rim within 20 km of the Shoemaker scarp
properties.observational_check: recent boulder falls on Shackleton's wall seen by ShadowCam; no recent regolith landslides observed where predicted (ice-raised cohesion suggested)

items.name: Planned seismic instruments
items.evidence: ESTABLISHED (selection); manifesting after the 2026 re-plan unknown

properties.LEMS: Artemis III deployed instrument selected Mar 2024: 3-axis short-period + 3-axis broadband, buried; 3 months to 2 years
properties.Farside_Seismic_Suite: Schrodinger basin, >= 4.5 months; status not confirmed

items.name: Mean slopes of major polar craters (20 m baseline)
Boulder populations near sites 001 (Connecting Ridge) and 004 (Shackleton rim)

properties.blocks: ~8 m blocks at the ridge-rim junction (-89.684, -163.261)

items.name: Generic design environment (DSNE): rocks and regolith depth

properties.rock_cover: rocks >~1 m typically ~1% of area but locally 10-20%

items.name: Narrow rims of de Gerlache and Nobile; Connecting Ridge approaches; Malapert relief

properties.statement: Rims of de Gerlache and Nobile are narrow and flanked by slopes unsuited to a stable landing; Connecting Ridge: slopes up to about 20 deg on rim approaches (low-reliability site); Malapert: summit >5,000 m above base, ~3,500 m cliff
Sub-km crater density drops strongly with slope (diffusive mass wasting); 250-500 m craters survive only ~3.5 Gyr even on plains

properties.notes: Coordinates are the IM-2 site as given in this note (29.1958; LROC value elsewhere 29.1957).
properties.IM-2: 6 Mar 2025, Mons Mouton: altimeter failed, struck a plateau, tipped, skidded, came to rest on its side in a ~20 m shadowed crater (~100 K); regolith coated solar panels
properties.IM-1: 22 Feb 2024, -80.13, 1.44: 12 deg slope, broke a leg, ~30 deg tilt
properties.common_cause: altimetry / navigation sensors, not slope or lighting directly (researcher inference)
properties.crewed_lander_concerns: Starship height -> tip-over risk; cryogenic propellants never used on the Moon; only one uncrewed landing test per provider

items.name: PSR surface porosity from LAMP far-UV albedo

properties.porosity: ~70% in PSRs vs ~40% outside (inferred, not measured)

items.name: PSR bearing capacity from boulder tracks (Sargeant et al. 2020)
items.limitations: Numeric kPa values not retrieved. No in-situ geotechnical measurement of PSR regolith exists.

properties.sample: 13 boulder tracks in shadowed terrain (70-76 deg latitude per one note; 'at/inside south-polar PSRs' per the other)
properties.result: 'somewhat stronger' than highland/mare at 0.28-1.00 m; statistically indistinguishable at 1-2 m; ice in pore space suggested

items.name: Slope-stability inputs used for the south pole

properties.isru_unknowns: cohesion 0-100 kPa; friction angle 10-50 deg; particle size 1-1000 um; bulk density 0.5-2.5 g/cm3; compressive strength 1-100 MPa (LWIMS design inputs still unknown)

items.name: Plume-surface interaction (PSI) for large landers
items.limitations: No validated crater-depth or ejecta-range numbers for Starship/Blue Moon found.

properties.statement: 'Apollo flight experience cannot be extrapolated to upcoming large Human Landing Systems'; subscale hybrid motor tests over regolith simulant; NASA Langley vacuum-chamber tests (BP-1 simulant) continue into 2026; lunar flight PSI data lacking
properties.chandrayaan_3: exhaust removed about 3 cm of regolith
properties.instrumentation: SCALPSS plume cameras on Blue Moon MK1 Endurance

items.name: Lander exhaust contaminating polar cold traps (Prem et al. 2020)

properties.result: water-vapour exhaust globally redistributed within hours; 30-40% remained in exosphere/surface after two months; roughly 20% ultimately freezes out near the poles; contamination scales with exhaust mass and proximity to the poles; water is only ~1/3 of typical exhaust
properties.nasem: most contaminants not expected to penetrate more than a few centimetres; mitigations: mission-specific exhaust modelling, characterised exhaust signatures, witness plates, sampling protocols

items.name: Dust lofting and charging
items.limitations: Surface-potential values (kV) not confirmed from a primary source.

properties.statement: Electrostatic lofting proposed for near-surface (<1 m, Surveyor) and high-altitude (1-100 km, Apollo) observations; Apollo LEAM terminator enhancement discounted (Grun and Horanyi 2011); LADEE/LDEX measured dust well below Apollo-era estimates; 'dynamic fountain' model: grains <0.1 um lofted ~1-100 km at terminator (open question); lighting and plasma environment 'more complex' at the poles

properties.context: far side, solar minimum; likely an upper limit for GCR; design environment: interplanetary GCR/SEP fluxes divided by 2 plus albedo neutrons

properties.shackleton_like_crater: 20 km simple crater (proxy for 'Artemis Base Camp 004' near the rim): SEP dose reduced >= 40% inside the crater and >= 10% just outside the rim relative to a flat plain (Geant4, Oct 1989 worst-case SEP)
properties.stubbs_2020: 20 km wide, 3 km deep crater cuts net exposure ~40%
properties.habitat_beside_wall: total dose -44.9% at 15 m depth, -10.7% at 5 m depth (PHITS)

properties.secondary: NASA SP-8013 (Apollo era) in SLS-SPEC-159 DSNE; replacement MeMoSeE predicts ejecta flux ~2-3 orders of magnitude lower for particles >1 ug

items.name: Cold and thermal extremes
items.limitations: Diviner summer-max / winter-min values for named features not retrieved from a primary source.

properties.psr: ~25 K in coldest polar PSRs (record on Hermite, north pole); Haworth coldest areas never exceed ~40 K; Shackleton floor ~88-90 K; PSR interiors down to -248 C; LCROSS site annual average 37 K; PSR floors below -410 F (~28 K) in places
properties.sunlit: illuminated near-rim sites at Shackleton about -50 +/- 10 C; NASA: above 54 C in sunlit areas to -203 C in PSRs
properties.slope_sensitivity: Chandrayaan-3 ChaSTE at 69.37 S: 355 K (+/-0.5) on ~6 deg Sun-facing slope vs ~332 K (+/-1) on flat ground ~1 m away
properties.eclipse_swing: ~5-hour eclipse took a mid-latitude surface from about +40 C to -170 C (press report)
properties.key_parameter: maximum time in shadow; at best sites 20-50% of a normal lunar night

properties.statement: Sun never above 7 deg in landing regions; crews cannot avoid Sun in their eyes; no existing requirement guaranteed functional vision moving between sunlight and shadow (NESC recommended one); shadows ~27x object height; deep shadows can hide large obstacles; Apollo 12 crew thought a ~10 deg slope was ~40 deg; Apollo 12 colour TV camera burned out pointed at a 7.5 deg Sun; in driving simulations crews tacked +/-20-30 deg to avoid glare; LIDAR suggested for hazard sensing
